funders.name: ICSSR Scheme for Participation in International Seminar/Conference Abroad
funders.eligible_who: PhD/postdoctoral scholars in social science disciplines (incl. media & communication, South Asian studies) at recognized Indian universities/institutes, in advanced stage of research; also regular faculty
funders.amount_note: Faculty: up to 50% of visit cost (airfare, visa, insurance, local conveyance, stay, registration up to US$200). PhD/PDF scholars and SC/ST/PwD faculty without other funding: full financial assistance.
funders.cycle: Rolling, apply online at least 3 months before the conference date; not considered after the conference has occurred
funders.requires: Formal acceptance letter from organizers (email invites insufficient), full paper to be presented, hard-copy application to ICG Division

funders.name: UGC Travel Grant Scheme (for conference/seminar abroad)
funders.eligible_who: Permanent college/university teachers, librarians, vice-chancellors and UGC officers presenting at foreign conferences — NOT open to PhD scholars directly
funders.amount_note: Covers admissible foreign travel, registration fee, per-diem, visa fee (exact cap not verified on current page)
funders.cycle: Apply to UGC Joint Secretary (Travel Grant) at least 2 months before the conference
funders.requires: Acceptance letter from organizers, copy/full text of paper being presented
funders.source_note: Underlying UGC guideline PDFs found are dated 2009; scheme is faculty-only, not a fit for a PhD scholar's own travel

funders.name: National Fellowship for Other Backward Classes (NFOBC) — contingency grant
funders.eligible_who: OBC-category, full-time M.Phil/PhD scholars in recognized Indian institutions with family income under Rs 6 lakh/year (caste/income-restricted, not universal)
funders.amount_note: Contingency grant: Rs 10,000/year (years 1-2), then Rs 20,500/year for Humanities & Social Sciences; separate from monthly stipend of Rs 25,000-28,000 + HRA. Contingency funds can be used toward travel/fieldwork/conference costs.
funders.cycle: Annual selection cycle via nfobc.ugc.ac.in; exact 2026-27 deadline not confirmed
funders.requires: OBC certificate, income certificate, PhD registration proof
funders.source_note: General fellowship contingency, not a dedicated travel grant; only applicable if the scholar qualifies under OBC/income criteria

funders.note: Home institution: check the university's research/dean-of-students or international-relations office for an internal PhD conference-travel fund; specific to the institution and not tracked here.

funders.name: Charles Wallace India Trust (CWIT) grants
funders.eligible_who: Indian citizens aged 28-45 in visual/performing arts, heritage conservation, history, literature, philosophy — NOT media studies/social-science PhD research or conference travel
funders.amount_note: Short Research Grants up to GBP 1,750 (for eligible arts/humanities fields only)
funders.cycle: Annual; 2026-27 long-term and short research grant cycles are listed as closed on the current page
funders.requires: Not applicable to this profile's field/purpose
funders.source_note: Real UK-India trust, but scope (arts/heritage professionals) does not cover a media-studies PhD's conference travel

funders.name: Shastri Indo-Canadian Institute — Scholar Travel Subsidy Grant (SSTSG)
funders.eligible_who: Indian and Canadian scholars/students building India-Canada research linkages (relevant only if destination is Canada or a Canada-linked event)
funders.amount_note: Travel subsidy amount not confirmed on current page
funders.cycle: 2025-26 cycle closed (deadline was 12 Oct 2025); 2026-27 cycle not yet announced
funders.requires: Institutional India-Canada linkage/application via SICI grants portal (sicigms.org)
funders.source_note: Only relevant if the conference/destination involves Canada; next cycle dates not yet posted

funders.name: IAMCR Travel Grants (for IAMCR annual conference)
funders.eligible_who: Early-career (untenured) IAMCR members of ≥1 year, residing in low/middle-income countries (India qualifies), first author of a paper accepted for full presentation at the IAMCR annual conference
funders.amount_note: Up to 18 grants, each max USD 2,000
funders.cycle: Annual, tied to each year's IAMCR conference; 2026 cycle (Galway) deadline was 20 March 2026 — apply early in the year for the next conference
funders.requires: Paper acceptance confirmation from section/working-group head, IAMCR membership, full paper by the stated deadline
funders.source_note: Directly relevant field society for media & communication research; recurring annual scheme

funders.name: Association for Asian Studies (AAS) — South Asia Council Conference Award
funders.eligible_who: AAS members accepted to present South Asia-related research at any AAS-affiliated conference (Annual Conference, AAS-in-Asia, AAS Regional Conferences) in 2026
funders.amount_note: Roughly 11 awards of USD 150 and 16 awards of USD 200 (small travel subsidies)
funders.cycle: Rolling for 2026; note the AAS2026 Vancouver funding cap has already been reached, so only AAS-in-Asia 2026 and AAS Regional Conferences 2026 remain open
funders.requires: AAS membership, conference acceptance on South Asia topic
funders.source_note: Page returned 403 to direct fetch; details corroborated via multiple independent search-result excerpts of the AAS site dated 2026, not a raw page fetch

funders.note: No current destination-specific scheme found for an Indian early-career humanities/social-science scholar traveling to the UK, US, Europe or Australia. The Australia-India Strategic Research Fund (AISRF) EMCR Fellowship runs in the opposite direction (Australian researchers visiting India) and is not a fit.
